metadata.title: Irish Policy Monitor — Research Register
metadata.editorial_status: Starter evidence register; not a complete policy audit
rules: Distinguish policy commitments, enacted measures, implementation outputs and population outcomes.
Attribute party proposals to the party publishing them; do not describe proposals as enacted policy.
For every indicator retain its definition, period, publication date, source URL and caveats.
Do not compare unlike international systems without explaining institutional differences.
Do not issue an overall success score without published criteria, weighting and uncertainty.

indicators.interpretation: Budget allocation context only; spending level is not evidence of service effectiveness.
indicators.caveat: Departmental functions and classifications can change between years.

indicators.interpretation: Completions increased from 30,136 in 2024 and 32,473 in 2023. This is a supply measure, not a direct measure of affordability or adequacy.
indicators.caveat: Need compare with household formation, vacancy, tenure, location, affordability and public/private mix.

indicators.interpretation: Stock of people awaiting a first hospital outpatient consultation at end-September 2026.
indicators.caveat: Waiting-list stock does not by itself describe clinical urgency, time waited, duplicates or patient outcomes. Pair with waiting-time bands and activity.

indicators.interpretation: Stock awaiting inpatient or day-case treatment at end-September 2026.
indicators.caveat: Interpret with waiting-time bands, case mix, admissions and treatment throughput.

indicators.interpretation: Provisional emissions fell 2.2% in 2025. EPA states that the 2030 national target remains very challenging and annual reductions need to accelerate.
indicators.caveat: 2025 data are provisional; LULUCF estimates and final inventory will be updated.

indicators.interpretation: CSO reports 19% in 2025 compared with 10% in 2019. Survey-based victimisation differs from police-recorded crime.
indicators.caveat: Personal crime includes violent and non-violent theft, fraud and physical assault; compare survey definitions and recall period.

indicators.indicator: Respondents viewing Gardaí as effective in tackling local crime
indicators.interpretation: CSO reports 57% in 2025, down from 68% in 2019.
indicators.caveat: Perception measure, not a direct measure of detection or clearance rates.

indicators.source: Department of Housing — September 2026 Homelessness Report
indicators.interpretation: The report records 12,168 adults and 5,897 children in emergency accommodation in September 2026.
indicators.caveat: This measure covers people in emergency accommodation and is not a complete count of all forms of homelessness or housing insecurity.

indicators.indicator: RTB/ESRI Rent Index — latest published series
indicators.type: Regulatory data independently analysed by ESRI
indicators.interpretation: The RTB/ESRI index tracks new and existing tenancy rents using registered tenancy data and standardises for property characteristics.
indicators.caveat: Load the actual Q1 2026 report tables before quoting a numerical rent level or growth rate.

indicators.source: Teagasc — Farm incomes to fall in 2026 as milk and cattle prices ease
indicators.interpretation: Teagasc forecast average family farm income around €33,600 in 2026, down 38% on the 2025 average of about €53,800.
indicators.caveat: Forecast, not final observed income; substantial variation between farm systems. Figures include support payments.

indicators.indicator: Rivers and lakes in good or better biological quality
indicators.interpretation: EPA reports just over half (54%) of rivers and lakes were in good or better biological quality; nutrient pressures remain significant.
indicators.caveat: The percentage is one indicator among several; water-body status, nutrient trends and ecological quality should be assessed together.

indicators.indicator: Average nitrogen levels at 20 representative river monitoring sites
indicators.interpretation: EPA reported average annual nitrogen levels at 20 representative sites increased by 10% in 2025 compared with 2024.
indicators.caveat: Monitoring-site sample and weather, inputs and land-management factors all matter; this is not a direct attribution of change to one policy.

indicators.interpretation: Q3 completions rose 10.4% compared with Q3 2025. Apartments were 3,464; scheme houses 5,163; single houses 1,527.
indicators.caveat: Quarterly completions are volatile. Compare rolling 12-month totals, regional distribution, affordability and household formation.

indicators.indicator: New dwelling completions in the 12 months to September 2026
indicators.source: Department of Housing — Monthly Housing Update November 2026
indicators.interpretation: The November update reports 38,792 completions in the 12 months to Q3 2026, up 18% on the equivalent prior period.
indicators.caveat: Departmental summary of CSO data; use CSO release for the underlying series and methodology.

indicators.indicator: Residential Property Price Index annual change
indicators.source: Department of Housing — Monthly Housing Update November 2026
indicators.interpretation: Residential property prices rose 5.1% in the 12 months to August 2026.
indicators.caveat: National annual price growth does not measure affordability relative to incomes, rents or regional differences.

indicators.interpretation: Ireland's population was estimated at 5.5 million in 2026. Between 2016 and 2026 the share aged 45 or over rose from 37.1% to 42.2%.
indicators.caveat: Population growth and ageing affect housing, health, education, labour supply and infrastructure demand; they are context, not policy outcomes.

indicators.interpretation: Employment rate was 74.6% in 2025, up from 64.8% in 2015 and above the EU27 average of 71.0%.
indicators.caveat: Employment rate alone does not measure pay adequacy, hours, job security, underemployment or regional differences.

indicators.indicator: Irish consumer price level relative to EU27 average
indicators.interpretation: Ireland had the second-highest consumer goods and services price level in the EU27 in 2025, 36.2% above the EU average.
indicators.caveat: Price level comparison is not the same as inflation. Income levels and purchasing power must also be considered.

indicators.interpretation: Ireland had the highest rate in the EU27 in 2025.
indicators.caveat: Qualification attainment does not directly measure literacy, numeracy, skills match, course quality or access inequalities.

indicators.indicator: Young people aged 18–24 not in employment, education or training
indicators.interpretation: Ireland's rate was the fifth-lowest in the EU27 and below the EU27 average of 11.8%.
indicators.caveat: Examine breakdowns by disability, gender, region, socioeconomic status and duration.

indicators.indicator: Male healthy life expectancy at birth
indicators.interpretation: Ireland ranked seventh in the EU27 for male healthy life expectancy in 2024.
indicators.caveat: Healthy life expectancy is a population measure, not a direct measure of access to care or avoidable waiting.

indicators.indicator: Female healthy life expectancy at birth
indicators.interpretation: Ireland ranked seventh in the EU27 for female healthy life expectancy in 2024.
indicators.caveat: Healthy life expectancy is a population measure, not a direct measure of access to care or avoidable waiting.

indicators.interpretation: Surplus was 1.8% of GDP in 2025, less than half the €23.4bn surplus in 2024, which included a €14.2bn one-off receipt linked to a CJEU ruling.
indicators.caveat: Irish fiscal aggregates are affected by multinational activity and volatile corporation tax; distinguish headline balance from structural fiscal capacity.

indicators.interpretation: Debt fell €5.6bn during 2025 and equalled 34.8% of GDP.
indicators.caveat: GDP is distorted by multinational activity; debt sustainability should also be assessed against GNI*, interest costs and future spending commitments.

indicators.indicator: Annualised assaults, threats, harassment and related offences
indicators.interpretation: Annualised recorded incidents were 4% higher than the 12 months to Q2 2025.
indicators.caveat: Recorded crime depends on reporting and recording practices; use alongside victimisation surveys, detection and court outcomes.

indicators.interpretation: Annualised recorded burglaries were 6% lower than the 12 months to Q2 2025.
indicators.caveat: Recorded crime depends on reporting and recording practices; compare with victimisation and detection data.

government_baseline.title: Programme for Government 2025 — Securing Ireland's Future
government_baseline.use: Baseline commitments across policy areas; individual commitments should be extracted with page references and owners.

government_baseline.title: Where Your Money Goes — 2026
government_baseline.use: Spending context and departmental allocations; pair with outturns and service outcomes.

party_alternatives.published: 2025/2026 budget cycle; verify document date on publisher page
proposals: Targeted second-tier child benefit and child-poverty measures
Increase state-funded social and affordable housing delivery
Weekly social welfare increases and income-tax/USC indexation
Additional child benefit and pension/welfare supports
More state-led affordable housing and modular housing capacity
Investment in Sláintecare, health staffing and disability services
Alternative approaches to housing supply, rents and tax credits
Health capacity and social protection proposals
party_alternatives.status: Party proposal; individual current policy pages and costings require verification
Secondary-source summary; obtain and cite original party document before treating details as fully verified

questions: What share is public or limited-profit?
What is the effect on affordability and supply?
international_comparators.caveat: Different constitutional, land, finance and planning systems limit direct transferability.

questions: How are primary and hospital care integrated?
What are waiting times and outcomes?
international_comparators.caveat: Compare age-adjusted outcomes, coverage, out-of-pocket costs and definitions.

questions: How are land use and transit planned together?
What is the rural service model?
How are projects appraised and delivered?
international_comparators.caveat: Population density, geography and existing network maturity differ.

questions: What grid, storage and interconnection investments are needed?
international_comparators.caveat: Generation mix, interconnection and industrial structure differ.

questions: How are teachers trained and retained?
How are inclusion and school funding organised?
international_comparators.caveat: Student demographics, school governance and selection practices differ.
